market.summary: A soft open is likely: GIFT Nifty was about 60-70 points below Thursday's Nifty close of 25,299 early this morning. Overnight, US stocks slipped about 0.4% after Nvidia's CEO resigned, US 10-year yields rose above 5.1% and oil firmed after Trump said he is no longer interested in a deal with Iran; India's October inflation came in at 6.09%, above the RBI's 6% ceiling. Against that, foreign investors keep buying heavily and Japan and Korea are up nearly 2% this morning, so the backdrop is mixed rather than weak.

points.text: GIFT Nifty near 25,232-25,253 before 8:30 IST, pointing to a Nifty open roughly 60-70 points lower.
12 Nov US close: S&P 500 -0.4% to 7,592, Dow -0.4% to 52,297, Nasdaq -0.4%, Russell 2000 -1.7%; Nvidia fell sharply after Jensen Huang's resignation and recovered part of the loss.
Foreign investors bought a provisional Rs 7,831 Cr of Indian shares on 12 Nov while domestic institutions sold Rs 6,331 Cr; November foreign inflows reach about Rs 75,400 Cr.
India's October CPI inflation rose to 6.09%, above the RBI's upper band of 6%; US 10-year yield about 5.12-5.13%.
Asia this morning: Nikkei +1.8%, KOSPI about +1.9-2.1%, Hang Seng -0.6%. Brent is quoted between about $92 (January futures) and $95 depending on the contract.

market.watch: Whether foreign buying absorbs a gap-down open; high inflation and 5%+ US yields are the risk for richly valued midcaps.
